editorial:
Picture a sunny Mediterranean city where a volunteer group called The Rescue is waiting for its new boss. Instead, they get Birgos, a former union leader who just broke out of an asylum with his friend Cleo. Everyone assumes he's the new director, and he just goes along with it. That mix-up kicks off a funny, warm story about second chances, mistaken identity, and people finding purpose in unexpected places. The vibe is light but thoughtful, with a gentle humor that keeps things moving without ever feeling heavy.

The acting is charming, especially the lead, who plays Birgos with a mix of confusion and quiet confidence. The pacing is steady, never rushing but never dragging. On the downside, some jokes land better than others, and a few side characters feel underused. Still, if you enjoy French comedies with heart, this one is a nice pick. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Birgos's true identity as an escaped asylum patient is revealed to the volunteers. Instead of turning him away, the group embraces him, recognizing the good he has done. Cleo also finds acceptance. The twist is that the mistake was never really a mistake at all, because Birgos becomes the leader they needed. The film ends on a hopeful note, with the association thriving under his unexpected guidance.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves French comedies with heart and mistaken-identity stories.
